scenario: Two friends are out for a walk in the park when one of them, One friend, trips and twists their ankle. They are in too much pain to walk.
learner_goal: Help your friend get to a medical facility (<extra_info>Extra information: Your friend needs immediate medical attention but cannot walk due to the pain.</extra_info>)
partner_goal: If your friend offers you help, accept their help and rationalize the cost of the ambulance (<extra_info>Extra information: You are worried about the cost of the ambulance, but you believe it's the safest way to get to a hospital.</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Ava—stay still, okay? That ankle looks bad; don’t try to stand. I’m calling an ambulance right now and I’ll stay with you—do you have any allergies or medications I should tell them?

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Okay—I'm staying still. No allergies and I'm not on any meds. Thank you for calling. I'm worried about how much an ambulance will cost, but you're right—it's the safest option, so please go ahead. Tell them my name is Ava Martinez, I'm 22, and that I twisted my ankle on the path. Please stay with me?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: They’re on the way — I gave them your name and location and they said about ten minutes. Stay completely still; I’ll sit behind you so you don’t have to move and I’ll prop your foot up on my jacket. Do you want me to gently remove your shoe or call anyone for you? I’ll cover whatever this costs — you need to get seen, Ava, I’m right here.

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Okay — thank you. I know ambulances are expensive and I'm worried about the bill, but you're right: it’s the safest option. I really appreciate you offering to cover it; we can sort out payment/insurance later. Please stay with me. Could you gently remove my shoe so they can check the swelling? And please call my roommate Maya to meet us at the hospital — tell them my name and where we are. Also let the EMTs know I have no allergies and no meds. Thank you, Ethan.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Okay — I’ll gently remove your shoe now; tell me if it hurts. Do you have Maya’s number or should I call from your phone? I’ll call her and tell the EMTs you have no allergies and no meds and exactly where we are. I’m right here with you.

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Yes — please call Maya. Her number is 555‑0142 (Maya Rivera). Tell her where we are and to meet us at the hospital. Thank you so much for covering the ambulance — I hate the cost, but getting checked is worth it; we can sort out payment/insurance later. You can gently remove my shoe now, and please tell me before you move it. Also tell the EMTs I have no allergies and take no meds. I really appreciate you, Ethan.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: [action] I’m calling Maya now (555‑0142) and telling her where we are and to meet you at the hospital. Okay—I’m going to gently remove your shoe now; I’ll warn you before I move it. Tell me immediately if you feel a sharp pain.

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Okay—I'm ready. Please warn me before you move my shoe. It's sore now, but I'll tell you immediately if it gets sharp. Thank you for calling Maya and for staying with me.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: [action] Warning — I'm going to gently remove your shoe now. (I support your ankle with both hands and carefully slip the shoe off.) Tell me immediately if you feel a sharp pain.

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Okay — it’s sore but not a sharp pain right now. Thank you for taking my shoe off and staying with me. Please prop my foot on your jacket and, if you can, put something cold (a water bottle wrapped in a jacket or a paper towel) against the swelling so it’s not directly on my skin. Tell Maya to bring my ID and insurance card to the hospital. I know ambulances are expensive, but getting checked is worth it — thank you again for covering it; we can sort out reimbursement later. Please stay with me until they arrive.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Okay — I’ve got your foot up on my jacket. I’ll grab a cold water bottle from my bag and wrap it in a paper towel/jacket before I set it gently on the swelling. I already called Maya and told her to bring your ID and insurance; she’s on her way. Tell me immediately if it gets sharp or you feel faint — I’m right here with you.

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Okay — that cold feels good, thank you. I’m really relieved Maya’s on her way. I appreciate you covering the ambulance; I hate the cost but you’re right — getting checked is worth it and we’ll sort out payment/insurance later, I promise I’ll pay you back. Please stay with me until the EMTs arrive and hold my hand if you can. Remind them again I have no allergies and take no meds when they get here. Thanks, Ethan.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: I’m right here — I’ll hold your hand. (I squeeze your hand gently and keep your foot propped.) I’ll remind the EMTs again about no allergies and no meds when they arrive. You’re doing great; stay still, help is almost here.

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Thanks, Ethan — I feel better with you here. Please keep holding my hand. When the EMTs get here, tell them my name (Ava Martinez, 22), where we are, that I twisted my ankle and it’s swollen, I have no allergies or meds, and to immobilize the ankle and check for a fracture before moving me. Maya’s on her way with my ID and insurance. I know ambulances are expensive, but getting checked is worth it — I’ll pay you back. Please stay with me until they take over.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson

I’m right here holding your hand; do you want me to grab anything else from your bag or text anyone else while we wait?

transcript.speaker: Ava Martinez
transcript.content: Please don't worry about grabbing anything else — just keep holding my hand and help me stay calm. Could you text Maya to say EMTs are almost here and we're staying put? Thank you so much for covering the ambulance; I know it's expensive but you're right — getting checked is worth it and I'll pay you back. Please stay with me until they take over.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson

When they get here please ask the EMTs to talk me through what they’re doing and to immobilize my ankle before moving me. Tell Maya to bring my ID and insurance. I really appreciate you being here — we’ll sort the money later and I’ll pay you back.
